newsitem.title: UK: Iraq sees eventual 8 mln bpd output capacity.
newsitem.headline: Iraq sees eventual 8 mln bpd output capacity.

text.p: Iraq could achieve a sustainable oil production capacity of about eight million barrels per day (bpd) but the current sanctions and political situation in the country cold put this off for "some years", a former Iraqi oil minister said on Tuesday.

Issam al-Chalabi, who was oil minister of Iraq when it invaded Kuwait in 1990, told the Oil and Money conference that the number of discovered but not appraised oil fields in Iraq surpasses that of any other country.

"In terms of production capabilities and based on detailed seismic and reservoir studies...Iraq could go up to a sustainable production capacity of around eight million bpd provided it had the financial means and technological capability," Chalabi said.
But Chalabi said there were a number of obstacles that will hamper Iraq's oil expansion. "I regret to say that I hold the pessimistic view at least for some years to come," he said.
Hit by U.N. sanctions four days after it invaded Kuwait in August 1990, Iraq is banned from selling its oil on world markets and currently produces only about 700,000 bpd.
The implementation of an oil-for-food deal by the U.N. which would have allowed for limited exports was suspended earlier this year after Iraq's armed incursion into its norther Kurdish province.

Chalabi said that Iraq has gone from being the second largest oil exporter in the world in 1990 to exporting only about two to three percent of its pre-invasion levels. That volume was moved to Jordan in semi-official exports and smuggled barrels, he said.

Chalabi, who was Iraqi oil minister from 1987 to late 1990, said that only a small part of Iraq has been explored for hydro-carbons. He said that those areas that were explored were done so without many of the new technological processes applied successfully in other oil regions.

"The recovery factors used for compliation of geological and reservoir studies for new fields and in determining production plateaus for producing fields range between 10-30 percent only with very limited exceptions," he said.
Iraq produced nearly 3.5 million bpd before it invaded Kuwait, with an estimated production capacity of 4.5 million bpd.
